LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The `makepkg --printsrcinfo` command only sources the PKGBUILD file and evaluates its top-level/global scope. In this PKGBUILD, the top-level scope contains only standard variable assignments (pkgname, pkgver, pkgrel, pkgdesc, arch, url, license, depends, conflicts, provides, makedepends, sha256sums, sha256sums_x86_64, source, source_x86_64) - all of which are benign.

The only code that would execute during sourcing is within the `package()` function, but this function is NOT called during `makepkg --printsrcinfo` as specified in the instructions. The function definition itself is just a binding and does not execute any code. There are no top-level command substitutions, network requests, file downloads, or system modifications in the global scope.

All the suspicious-looking patterns mentioned in the context (like network requests, obfuscated code, dangerous commands) are either in comments or inside the `package()` function, which is out of scope for this specific safety gate.
</details>
<evidence>

</evidence>
<summary>
No malicious code in top-level scope; all code is in package() function
</summary>
</security_assessment>
